ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Higuchi Ichiyō

code.originalText: End of the eight-week intensive phase: susceptibility results, the two-month sputum culture, and the start of the continuation phase

text.paragraph: End of the eight-week intensive phase. [S]

Ms. Higuchi returns at the end of the intensive phase, having taken all 56 doses by video, the last pyrazinamide dose yesterday. The isolate was susceptible to isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, and ethambutol was stopped by phone three weeks ago when the result arrived. The two-week sputum showed no acid-fast bacilli, and its culture has had no growth. The cough has gone and the night sweats stopped a month ago. She has no nausea, yellowing, dark urine, abdominal pain, numbness, or change in vision. She is eating well and has gained 2.5 kg. She is writing two hours each morning and has sent a story to an editor. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-06-12; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Looks well; weight 41.0 kg, BMI 18.7; temperature 36.8 °C, pulse 80
No icterus. Visual acuity 85 letters in each eye; Ishihara plates normal

Cough for about seven weeks with evening fevers, night sweats, poor appetite and weight loss of about 4 kg (about 10 percent) in a woman of 23; chest X-ray with patchy right upper lobe opacities and no cavity; suspected pulmonary tuberculosis; airborne precautions and three sputum specimens for acid-fast smear, nucleic acid amplification and culture
S — Synthetic presenting problem at intake, superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit; its timing echoes her documented decline from early 1896 (D).
Pulmonary tuberculosis of the right upper lobe, sputum smear-negative, confirmed by Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra (Mycobacterium tuberculosis detected, low; rifampin resistance not detected)
S — Synthetic modern coding of her documented tuberculosis; all bacteriology and imaging are synthetic.
Moderate protein-calorie malnutrition: BMI 17.6, about 10 percent weight loss in two months, and albumin 3.3 g/dL
S — Synthetic nutrition diagnosis at intake, anchored to her documented poverty.
Low and irregular income from writing, with a household to support; costs of care are a barrier
S — Synthetic social need anchored to her documented poverty and household responsibilities.

list.item:
Pulmonary tuberculosis, drug-susceptible, end of the intensive phase (A15.0). Excellent clinical response with full adherence. ALT 26, AST 25, bilirubin 0.5, all normal. Without a cavity on the first X-ray, the continuation phase is four months. If the two-month culture were positive, extension to seven months would be considered because she is underweight; it is not changed while that culture is pending. [S]
Isoniazid 200 mg, rifampin 450 mg and pyridoxine 50 mg daily by video-observed therapy for eighteen weeks from today.
Pyrazinamide finished yesterday.
Induced sputum today for the two-month smear and culture.
In the continuation phase, liver tests only for symptoms, since the tests stayed normal and albumin has recovered; the observing nurse asks about symptoms at each dose.

Moderate protein-calorie malnutrition, improving (E44.0). Weight 41.0 kg and albumin 3.8 g/dL; hemoglobin 12.4 g/dL, up from 11.4 as the infection settles. [S]
Continue the meal plan and supplement drinks.

Missed: the liver tests due about four weeks into treatment were not drawn, because no visit was booked and the phone call that stopped ethambutol did not include a blood test. No harm judging by today's normal results and the absence of symptoms at every observed dose. Corrective action: blood tests due between visits are now booked as laboratory visits with a reminder to the observing nurse
Baseline and monthly while on ethambutol

Missed: the monthly vision check due about four weeks into treatment, while she was still taking ethambutol, was not done for the same reason. No harm: acuity 85 letters in each eye and normal color vision today, three weeks after ethambutol was stopped. Corrective action: any future ethambutol course is booked with monthly vision checks

Follow-up: Two-month culture result by phone. Preventive visit as booked. End-of-treatment visit after the 182nd dose. Call for cough, fever, weight loss, hepatitis symptoms or numbness. Next scheduled visit 2026-08-24: periodic adult preventive visit. [S]
